entries.title: Zelensky should be asked what he knew about government corruption, sacked minister tells BBC
entries.snippet: Mykhailo Fedorov has also called for wartime elections to be held in Ukraine.

entries.title: Trump says Canada wants 'benefits' of being US state after trade talks collapse
entries.snippet: Canada's PM said he was "reluctantly" announcing retaliatory tariffs and accused the US of starting a trade war.

entries.title: Guinea rubbish landfill collapse kills 30
entries.snippet: A mound of rubbish at a major waste site buried several homes in the capital, the government says.

entries.title: DR Congo and M23 rebels agree roadmap for peace talks
entries.snippet: Representatives met in Switzerland to work out next steps to resolve the conflict.

entries.title: France links sharp rise in drownings to heatwaves
entries.snippet: A government minister says people have been taking risks by going into the water, with 301 deaths since 19 June.

entries.title: Dozens of co-ordinated arson attacks hit southern Thailand
entries.snippet: No group has claimed responsibility for the attacks, which the military said "aimed at creating unrest".

entries.title: Trump waves green flag to start IndyCar race through Washington streets
entries.snippet: The president took a ceremonial lap of the track before the race, which is the culmination of a summer of events to mark the country's 250th birthday.

entries.title: Frustration builds in Indiana town struggling without power for 12 days
entries.snippet: In the town of Gary, where a third of residents live in poverty, people say they have been living in "survival mode".

entries.title: Kejelcha breaks men's half marathon world record by 29 seconds
entries.snippet: Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha breaks the men's half marathon world record in a time of 56 minutes 51 seconds in a World Athletics road race in Buenos Aires.

entries.title: Golf brand apologises for advert that shows woman being pushed over
entries.snippet: Content creator Good Good apologises and removes an advert that shows a woman being pushed to the ground as she reached for a man's golf club.

entries.title: 'We're not going to run from it': Sydney Marathon laughs off medal error
entries.snippet: Runners will receive a medal at the 2026 Sydney Marathon with an engraving of a German stadium.

entries.title: 'New season, new trim' - Haaland reveals buzzcut
entries.snippet: Manchester City striker Erling Haaland reveals his new buzz cut on social media.

entries.title: Girl, 17, killed in Swedish sword attack, police say
entries.snippet: Two boys aged 12 and 17 were also injured, while an 18-year-old suspect has been detained.

entries.title: Man completes 2,800 mile scoot across Australia
entries.snippet: Bob Brown from Saltash has ridden a non-electric scooter from Perth to Sydney.

entries.title: Father leaves 7-year-old son alone on Mount Fuji to continue hike
entries.snippet: The man had taken his two boys on the trip but is said to have left one behind when he got tired.

entries.title: Syria says Israeli strike near Damascus violation of international law
entries.snippet: The latest incident comes days after reports emerged Israel had struck a military airbase close to the Turkish border.

entries.title: Rescuers dig through Ukraine mall wreckage as Zelensky condemns 'despicable' Russian strike
entries.snippet: Four people are still missing after Friday's attack which killed 16 and left 130 injured, including a number of children.

entries.title: Fourteen killed in strike on Myanmar monastery
entries.snippet: A rescue worker said the site had been struck twice as civilians gathered for a meditation retreat.

entries.title: US military newspaper editor voices censorship fears after being fired
entries.snippet: Erik Slavin believes he was fired for saying in an interview that "in a hypothetical situation, censorship would be a red line".

entries.title: TikTok to pay $400m to US in one of largest child privacy settlements
entries.snippet: The deal stems from a 2024 lawsuit alleging TikTok and its parent company ByteDance collected "vast amounts of data" on millions of users under the age of 13.

entries.title: Thousands in northwest Indiana still without power nearly two weeks after storm
entries.snippet: A round of storms impacted the region on Aug. 11

entries.title: Nonprofits are helping musicians pay for insurance in Austin, Texas, and beyond
entries.snippet: A nonprofit and a local public health agency are subsidizing marketplace health insurance for Austin musicians , even as rising healthcare costs make the program more expensive.

entries.title: Becerra, running for governor of California, faces a health insurance problem
entries.snippet: The nation's uninsured rate hit a historical low when Xavier Becerra was health secretary. Now he wants to be California's next governor as Trump's actions have driven people off health insurance.

entries.title: Tropical Storm Moke to cause more flooding as Hawaii recovers from Lala
entries.snippet: More than a foot of rain could fall across Big Island of Hawaii, according to NOAA.

entries.title: Body cam shows federal agent was 'unjustified' in Memphis shooting, attorney says
entries.snippet: The family of Jonah Neal and their attorney were recently shown video from the day that Neal was shot by a federal agent while he experienced a mental health crisis.

entries.title: Trump administration's 75-country visa ban was illegal, judge rules
entries.snippet: The U.S. stopped issuing visas for citizens of 75 countries because it said they were likely to need public assistance. A judge ruled the policy illegally discriminated on the basis of nationality.

entries.title: Opinion: Mr. Rogers keeps finding a new neighborhood
entries.snippet: MLB catcher Jake Rogers probably didn't know if he was coming or going the last several weeks: he's been a Detroit Tiger, a Baltimore Oriole, a Boston Red Sox, and now he's a Chicago White Sox.

entries.title: As Flock battles public scrutiny, other police surveillance companies see an opening
entries.snippet: Dozens of cities have canceled their contracts with Flock. Some are switching to other companies, but privacy experts say they're no better than Flock.

entries.title: As Canada readies retaliatory tariffs, Mark Carney says his nation is 'at war' with U.S.
entries.snippet: The U.S. has now imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products. Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada will match those tariffs "dollar for dollar" starting Sept. 8.

entries.title: A battle over 'Italian brainrot' could shape who owns AI art
entries.snippet: A legal battle over what looks like a cartoon stick could help set the rules over whether creators can claim ownership of their AI-generated characters.

entries.title: He was waiting for his son to return from the USS Lincoln. Then Border Patrol arrested him.
entries.snippet: Luis Manuel Aviles, 48, was arrested after leaving his house to take his car to the mechanic, according to his wife, Argelia Aviles. She said her husband, a handyman in Key West, Florida, has a permit to work in the United States.

entries.title: Human-caused wildfire approaches Reno, Nevada, forcing thousands of evacuations
entries.snippet: The Hawk Fire began Saturday and quickly grew to 20 square miles as it spread across the Peavine Peak area of the Humboldt–Toiyabe National Forest, where rugged foothills are ringed by homes and businesses near the California state line.

entries.title: Report: Jared Kushner and Democratic leader Jeffries meet with House control at stake in November
entries.snippet: The meeting, first reported Sunday by The New York Times, touched on issues ranging from housing, immigration to the high costs of living.

entries.title: Zelenskyy details rift with Ukraine's dismissed defense minister Fedorov
entries.snippet: Zelenskyy said that he believes actions taken by dismissed Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, including his involvement in mass protests and calls for an election, were misguided, as he publicly detailed their dispute for the first time.

entries.title: Indonesian police arrest 72 people suspected of starting forest fires
entries.snippet: Indonesia has been battling fires driven by an intensifying El Niño pattern and a prolonged dry season, generating dense smoke that crossed into Malaysia, according to Indonesia's National Disaster Management Agency.

entries.title: Tropical Storm Moke set to dump more heavy rain on hurricane-stricken Hawaii
entries.snippet: Forecasters expected Moke to produce as much as 10 inches of total rain across the Big Island, and up to 15 inches in some isolated places, enough to cause life-threatening flooding and mudslides for the windward and southeast slopes.

entries.title: Texas judge denies Karmelo Anthony's request for new trial in deadly stabbing at track meet
entries.snippet: Judge Michael Chitty denied the retrial motion in a half-page order following a two-day hearing this week near Dallas, citing a review of the evidence and arguments. He did not elaborate.

entries.title: As the Lindsay Clancy case highlights postpartum psychosis, a mom stricken by it shares her story of hope
entries.snippet: Researchers estimate that the condition — a mental health emergency that is less common than postpartum depression — afflicts 1 to 2 out of 1,000 women after delivery.

entries.title: Carney warned about economic coercion. Now Trump is testing the Canadian prime minister
entries.snippet: For Carney, the showdown is the clearest test yet of his argument that middle powers must stand up to economic pressure from great powers such as the United States and China, even when it comes at a cost.

entries.title: Iran's president says U.S. memorandum is best path out of stalled war, and other Middle East news
entries.snippet: The new head of Iran's top security body warned Sunday that Tehran will see any country's support for new U.S. economic measures against the Islamic Republic as an "act of war," while Iran's president defended a memorandum of understanding with the U.S. as the best way out of the

entries.title: Trump waves the green flag to start the IndyCar race as racers zoom through Washington's streets
entries.snippet: The open-wheel race, with cars whizzing past Washington's monuments at speeds approaching 200 mph, is the latest of Trump's celebrations this year to mark America's 250th birthday.

entries.title: What to know about Trump's 50% tariffs on Canadian goods that just went into effect
entries.snippet: The new levies are expected to affect about 5% of Canada's annual exports to the U.S., roughly $20 billion in goods ranging from hockey sticks to agricultural products.

entries.title: Enriched uranium stockpile undercuts Trump claim of Iran's 'essential denuclearization'
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump said he has presided over "the essential denuclearization of Iran." But Iran likely still has materials and machinery that can be used to make nuclear weapons, undercutting Trump's claim.

entries.title: Tropical Storm Moke advances toward Hawaii as winds strengthen
entries.snippet: As with Hurricane Lala, the Big Island is expected to bear the brunt of Moke's rain and heavy winds as it passes south of a direct hit late Saturday into early Sunday.

entries.title: This rare Nebraska district backed Harris but sent a Republican to Congress. Can Democrats win here?
entries.snippet: Retiring Rep. Don Bacon's open seat pits fellow Republican and Omaha City Councilmember Brinker Harding against Democratic activist Denise Powell.

entries.title: Trump threatens lawsuit against nonprofit that questioned whether National Guard plan lessened crime
entries.snippet: The letter gave the Washington, D.C.-based Center for American Progress until the end of business Friday to issue the retraction or face a $5 billion lawsuit. The center declined.

entries.title: Student killed in sword attack at a Swedish school was a 17-year-old girl
entries.snippet: An 18-year-old man armed with a sword carried out the attack at the Brinell School in Fagersta, northwest of Stockholm, while classes were in session on Friday. One person was killed and three others were wounded, two of them severely.

entries.title: TikTok reaches $400 million settlement with Justice Department over children's privacy
entries.snippet: The DOJ said Friday that TikTok will pay $300 million immediately and another $100 million after an order vacates an earlier consent decree against its predecessor company, Musical.ly.

entries.title: Federal judge vacates Trump policy that suspended processing of immigration visas from 75 countries
entries.snippet: The judge ruled that Secretary of State Marco Rubio exceeded his authority by issuing the policy, which "runs afoul" of the Immigration and Nationality Act by mandating "the refusal of visas to eligible applicants without any basis in law."

entries.title: Federal officials announce water cuts as Colorado River supplies continue to plunge
entries.snippet: Under the Bureau of Reclamation's plan, California, Nevada and Arizona will collectively reduce water use by 1.25 million acre-feet annually for the next two years, with the possibility of larger cuts depending on conditions.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Kazakhstan parliamentary vote cements president's power
entries.snippet: Candidates from seven state-approved parties took part in the election, while opposition parties were banned. As Central Asia's largest nation, Kazakhstan maintains a delicate balance between Russia and the West.

entries.title: Zelenskyy repeats Ukraine not behind Nord Stream attack
entries.snippet: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was assisting German authorities with their investigation into the Nord Stream explosions. A second Ukrainian national was arrested in connection with the blasts.

entries.title: Greece: Migrants clash with police at detention center
entries.snippet: Clashes broke out between police and people at a migrant detention center in northern Greece, with 35 having escaped the facility before half of them were detained again.

entries.title: Guinea: Garbage collapse at landfill kills dozens
entries.snippet: Heavy seasonal rains caused a mound of garbage to collapse, burying dozens of people and nearby homes before the break of dawn.

entries.title: Iran: President defends deal with US as best option for peace
entries.snippet: Iran's president has said the country's economy needs a peace deal to attract investors. The Foreign Ministry said Pakistan's top army official will visit Tehran Monday as Islamabad seeks to mediate a resolution.

entries.title: Could Russia's growing fuel crisis help end the Ukraine war?
entries.snippet: Empty pumps, long waits: Attacks on oil refineries have left Russia increasingly short of fuel. Dissident Russian economists say growing anger about shortages among ordinary Russians could help end the Ukraine war.

entries.title: Congo, M23 rebels agree to peace roadmap
entries.snippet: Negotiators representing the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda-backed M23 rebels have agreed to a roadmap for peace. The US State Department, a mediator, released a joint statement.

entries.title: Harry Kane named footballer of the year in Germany
entries.snippet: Harry Kane has added another honor after a remarkable season for Bayern Munich and a strong World Cup with England. Bayern also took the top prize in coaching, and the club's Giulia Gwinn won women's Player of the Year.

entries.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy rejects wartime elections
entries.snippet: The Ukrainian president says wartime elections, as called for by the ex-defense minister, could "split Ukraine." He also said Russia was planning to mobilize hundreds of thousands of troops after September polls there.

entries.title: Is the US seeing a turning point in obesity rates?
entries.snippet: Obesity rates climbed in the US for years, but now there are signs this could be changing. Use of weight-loss drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy has increased rapidly — are they helping?

entries.title: What is the 'political firewall' against Germany's far-right AfD?
entries.snippet: Germany's centrist parties reject any cooperation with the Alternative for Germany (AfD), parts of which are classified as right-wing extremist. However, this policy is coming under increasing pressure.

entries.title: Search resumes for 22 crew after cargo ship sinks off India
entries.snippet: The Panama‑flagged Ocean Winner had 24 people on board when it sank in the Bay of Bengal. The ship is thought to have been carrying iron ore from India to Singapore.

entries.title: Trump hits out at Canada over retaliatory tariffs
entries.snippet: Donald Trump has accused Canada of treating US farmers unfairly for years as a trade standoff between Ottawa and Washington escalates. Both sides are threatening new tariffs after the collapse of talks on Friday.

entries.title: Australia confirms H5N1 bird flu case in local mammal
entries.snippet: Australian authorities said the deadly virus's spread to mammals was "concerning" but "not unexpected."

entries.title: Sydney Marathon medal wrongly shows German landmark
entries.snippet: A medal minted for finishers in the Sydney Marathon features a skyline of the city — with one landmark from rather far away. Organizers say the muddle only makes the medal "a little more unique."

entries.title: Ukraine: Could ex-defense minister challenge Zelenskyy?
entries.snippet: Last week, former Ukrainian defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov released a video in which he spoke of corruption, a crisis of leadership and elections. His explosive remarks have sparked widespread public debate.

entries.title: Mexican governor facing US drug charges says leaving office
entries.snippet: Embroiled in drug trafficking charges, Ruben Rocha Moya has asked for another leave of absence just days after returning to his position as Sinaloa state governor.

entries.title: Kazakhstan's future after the elections: Russia, EU or China
entries.snippet: Kazakhstan, where power is being continuously consolidated in the president's hands, will have to continue its tough balancing act between the EU, Russia and China following the parliamentary elections this Sunday.

entries.title: Iran warns countries against joining US 'economic war'
entries.snippet: Iran has said nations joining US economic sanctions against it would be considered enemies. Earlier this week, President Trump had announced what he called the "most crushing economic operation" against Tehran.
